newsitem.title: USA: SC Bancorp should be sold - shareholder.
newsitem.headline: SC Bancorp should be sold - shareholder.

text.p: Franklin Mutual Advisers Inc, unit of Franklin Resources Inc, said Thursday it has told SC Bancorp's management and board of directors that it believes the bank should be sold.
The group holds 401,700 common shares or 5.4 pct of SC Bancorp's outstanding common.
In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Franklin said it based its opinion in part on SC Bancorp's "mediocre financial performance."
Franklin said it would be unwilling to rely on SC Bancorp's "present management as the driver of an acquisition strategy, even at prices at levels less than the ones prevailing currently."
SC Bancorp, based in Anaheim, Calif., closed trading today at 9-5/8 per share.

In the filing, Franklin also argued the bank's common stock has traded at a significant discount to other financial insitutions until the recent rumors concerning the bank itself being a possible takeover candidate.
Based in San Mateo, Calif, Franklin Resources Inc's primary business is the Franklin Templeton Group with over $169 billion in assets under management.
